newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela link to Mercosur to take time - minister.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela link to Mercosur to take time - minister.

text.p: Venezuela's intention to form a free trade area with South America's largest customs bloc, Mercosur, will take a long time before it can come into effect, Development Minister Freddy Rojas Parra said.
"More than difficult, I see it as a long process...it could take quite a few months from December onwards," Rojas Parra told Reuters in an interview late on Thursday.

Rojas Parra, who is also president of Venezuela's Foreign Trade Institute (ICE), said Venezuela and its Andean Community partners -- Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia and Peru -- hoped to sign a preliminary accord with Mercosur in Brazil in December.
"The five members of the Andean Community are going to take a united position to the Mercosur members in December to define the base accord of the common general rules," he said.
This would include items such as procedures for the solution of disputes, clauses to protect domestic industry and a general outline for the reduction of tariffs.
"After that each country...taking into account its own particularities begins to negotiate a free trade zone with Mercosur...This will take time."
Rojas Parra acknowledged that apart from strong bilateral trade of over $2.5 billion per year with Colombia, trade with regional partners has been lower than expected.

Trade with Mexico, despite the Group of Three accord which also includes Colombia, has been slow to take off partly because Mexico has been concentrating more on the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
Also, "Venezuelan businessman have not taken the initiative to go out exploring markets in these areas," he added.

The unification of the Development Ministry and ICE to form a new Trade and Industry Ministry in December and the creation of a Foreign Trade Bank with a starting capital of $200 million next April are two government initiatives aimed at boosting trade.
